You are agent **J** on Katalyst stack 04 — you join the canvas to the engine. First read, fully, the shared brief at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/briefs/04-common.md` and follow everything in it. Then this.

**Your worktree:** `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04a-join` · **branch:** `feat/04a-join` · **base:** `spec/04a-streaming-growth`. You may commit on this branch. Do not push. **Ports, yours alone:** backend 8041, frontend 5141. **Scratch directory for screenshots and throwaway scripts:** `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kentgang-git3-katalyst/ef0fe818-4a51-417f-a20d-5479dc442258/scratchpad/j-shots/` (create it; nothing from it goes in the repo).

**Your pull request section in the plan:** "04a pull request 2 — the join", plus the paragraph "Drift stack 03 left for this stack" near the end of the plan (four items, all yours). Also read `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §7 in full, NFR-1, INV-8, INV-12; decision record 0014 (the computed chip's label and sentence, word for word); every merged chapter in `spec/workbench/` — especially `diff-view.md` (the `WorldSource` seam, `WorldView`, the structural states), `inspector.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md` — and `spec/multiverse/diff.md`; round-2 decisions K2, K3, K4, K5, K10 closely; then the code: `frontend/src/world/**`, `frontend/src/graph/diff/**`, `frontend/src/components/**`, `frontend/src/App.tsx`, `frontend/src/api/client.ts` and the generated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` (read only), and on the server `backend/src/katalyst/api/` (the three world routes and the 422 body) so you know exactly what answers.

**Files you own, and only these:** `frontend/src/world/**`, `frontend/src/components/**`, `frontend/src/graph/diff/**`, `frontend/src/App.tsx`, and their tests. You may add a call wrapper in `frontend/src/api/client.ts` if the three routes need one — say so in your report. **Never edit `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`, any Python file, any stylesheet token you do not need (if a new token is truly needed, add it to `styles/tokens.css` and justify it in the report), or anything under `spec/`.** Do not build the stream reader, the input bar or growth — that is the next pull request.

**What to build** is the plan section, exactly: `ApiWorldSource` stops throwing and asks the three routes; `App.tsx` hands the canvas an `ApiWorldSource` and falls back to `FixtureWorldSource` when the world route fails, **saying so on screen**; every slot in the plan's "What fills in" table; the six buttons append an edit and ask for a new world and a new diff (**Split this claim** stays visibly not live; **Add a claim** says plainly it needs the next pull request); a refused branch (422) shows every reason at once; the browser's structural states become a hint with the engine's affected set as the authority, pinned by `test_the_browser_states_agree_with_the_engine` (un-skip the existing skipped test as this); the conditional on a wire's midpoint fetched lazily and cached per `(branch, seed, link)`; the retraction badge read off `World.retractions`. Use the test names in the plan exactly, and do the four drift items (test renames to the chapters' snake_case names; rewrite `apiSource.ts`'s stale header; the un-skip; finish the `Known<T>` naming where the join touches it).

**One part waits.** Decision G3's Inspector sentence — *"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."* — reads a field that agent F is adding to the engine's diff right now on another branch. **Do not invent that field.** Build everything else, leave a clearly marked seam where the sentence will go, and say so in your report; the coordinator will rebase your branch onto F's fix and resume you. For the same reason `test_this_happened_puts_rows_on_the_rail` may not pass yet against today's engine (an observation currently leaves the rail empty — that is the bug F is fixing); write it, mark it as waiting on F's fix with a one-line reason, and list it in your report.

**The interface is the point.** No spinner anywhere, no pop-up dialog, no layout jump when numbers arrive, nothing conveyed by colour alone, two significant figures with the certainty guard (`>.99`, `<.01`), the rail never reorders or re-ranks what the engine sent. While a world is being fetched, the slots keep their honest absence — decide the wording from `spec/vocabulary.md`'s "Words for a number that is not there" and say which you used. Launch both halves (`cd backend && env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run uvicorn katalyst.api.main:app --port 8041`; `cd frontend && KATALYST_API_URL=http://localhost:8041 npm run dev -- --port 5141 --strictPort`), screenshot **every state you built** at 1600 × 1000 — base world with computed chips, the strike branch with `shifted` tiles and the ranked rail, a hovered wire with its conditional, a refused edit with all its reasons, the fallback with the server stopped, the Inspector's full decomposition — in both light and dark themes, and run the twelve-line visual review checklist on your own pictures. Also run `npx playwright test` (it starts both halves itself) and fix the existing end-to-end test if the join changes what it sees — without typing in any engine number.

Report in the shared format, with the paths of your screenshots and one line per checklist item.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, Claude publishes it. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks Claude to make the decision itself, such as "should we ship this?", Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector instead of publishing an artifact, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or an HTML or Markdown file. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and favicon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. The one exception is a workshop document from the `workshop` skill, which carries its own design: there Claude skips `artifact-design` and loads `artifact-diagramming` for a template page's diagrams. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open, in their organization.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: One or two emoji for the browser-tab icon (e.g. "📊"), with no markup. Required on a page's first publish. On a redeploy Claude omits it so the artifact keeps its icon, and passes a new one only when the person asks. Optional with `type_url` and for a typed Artifact's data files.

icon.description: Optional. One short generic word for the artifact's tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map — a plain signifier, not a product or brand name. Omit when republishing to keep the current icon. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open in the same organization, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact and it must be in your organization.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to types whose title or description contains this text, ignoring case. Omitting it lists them all.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai URL. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, which must be one the person owns; Claude omits it for a new artifact or a redeploy in the same conversation (see **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**). For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). content.content:
1	This is a take home coding assignment for https://catalyst.app/.
2	
3	Catalyst is the agent layer for finance. We turn natural language — a thesis, strategy, hedge, or trading idea — into live execution across any market, venue, or asset class from prediction markets to commodities to tokens to private markets. It is a seed stage company with investments from Sequoia, Jump Trading, and Lux Capital.
4	
5	Here are more details about Catalyst: https://coastalhq.co/scoop/e3a34548-1964-4b30-96ea-52801a558dd2
6	
7	The goal of the project is to create a functional protoype of the concept behind Catalyst as a company. The full brief I was provided for this is located at ./ASSIGNMENT.md
8	
9	## Map
10	
11	| Where | What |
12	|-------|------|
13	| `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | The compressed seed: decisions, requirements, invariants, anti-patterns, roadmap as PR stacks |
14	| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | The technical counterpart: layers, data flow, where each invariant is enforced, runtime, testing. Living; marks each section built or planned |
15	| `docs/adr/` | Numbered decision records (MADR format: context, options, decision, consequences); `template.md`; `README.md` index. Higher number supersedes |
16	| `spec/` | The spec as a book: one directory per idea (`graph/`, `multiverse/`, `thesis/`, `generation/`, `workbench/`, `probes/`), each with a landing page; `vocabulary.md` is the shared language |
17	| `docs/research/` | Four independent research reports (2026-09-16) that fed the PRD; inputs, not decisions |
18	| `plans/` | **Local only, git-ignored.** Agent-to-agent handoffs, working notes, orchestration. Start at `plans/README.md`. Nothing here is a source of truth — anything durable moves into a root document, a decision record, or the spec |
19	| `docs/initial-brainstorming.md` | Kent's raw notes; the origin of trigger/sustain links and refinement |
20	| `backend/` | The Python server. `domain/` is the pure core — the rules of the map and the arithmetic that works a change through it, no network, no model, no clock — and it is property-tested against maps nobody wrote by hand. `engine/` builds a world from a map, a branch and a seed; `api/` serves it |
21	| `frontend/` | The browser app: the canvas that draws a map, the wires, the Inspector, the two-world overlay and the keyboard. It reads the stored example today and is not joined to the engine yet. `src/api/schema.ts` is generated from the server's own description of itself and is never edited by hand; `e2e/` holds the one end-to-end test |
22	
23	## Working agreements (interview, 2026-09-16)
24	
25	* **ADR-gated cadence.** An agent drafts the ADR and spec first; Kent accepts, rejects, or amends; only then is code written. Nothing is implemented against a `proposed` ADR. Decisions Kent has already taken are listed in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3 — do not re-litigate them.
26	* **Disgust veto.** Two conditions end a line of work immediately: a template-looking UI, and any state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule, or a cited source.
27	* **Vocabulary is the interface.** Use `spec/vocabulary.md` words exactly in docs, code, and UI copy.

This is a take home coding assignment for https://catalyst.app/.

Catalyst is the agent layer for finance. We turn natural language — a thesis, strategy, hedge, or trading idea — into live execution across any market, venue, or asset class from prediction markets to commodities to tokens to private markets. It is a seed stage company with investments from Sequoia, Jump Trading, and Lux Capital.

Here are more details about Catalyst: https://coastalhq.co/scoop/e3a34548-1964-4b30-96ea-52801a558dd2

The goal of the project is to create a functional protoype of the concept behind Catalyst as a company. The full brief I was provided for this is located at ./ASSIGNMENT.md

## Map

| Where | What |
|-------|------|
| `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | The compressed seed: decisions, requirements, invariants, anti-patterns, roadmap as PR stacks |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | The technical counterpart: layers, data flow, where each invariant is enforced, runtime, testing. Living; marks each section built or planned |
| `docs/adr/` | Numbered decision records (MADR format: context, options, decision, consequences); `template.md`; `README.md` index. Higher number supersedes |
| `spec/` | The spec as a book: one directory per idea (`graph/`, `multiverse/`, `thesis/`, `generation/`, `workbench/`, `probes/`), each with a landing page; `vocabulary.md` is the shared language |
| `docs/research/` | Four independent research reports (2026-09-16) that fed the PRD; inputs, not decisions |
| `plans/` | **Local only, git-ignored.** Agent-to-agent handoffs, working notes, orchestration. Start at `plans/README.md`. Nothing here is a source of truth — anything durable moves into a root document, a decision record, or the spec |
| `docs/initial-brainstorming.md` | Kent's raw notes; the origin of trigger/sustain links and refinement |
| `backend/` | The Python server. `domain/` is the pure core — the rules of the map and the arithmetic that works a change through it, no network, no model, no clock — and it is property-tested against maps nobody wrote by hand. `engine/` builds a world from a map, a branch and a seed; `api/` serves it |
| `frontend/` | The browser app: the canvas that draws a map, the wires, the Inspector, the two-world overlay and the keyboard. It reads the stored example today and is not joined to the engine yet. `src/api/schema.ts` is generated from the server's own description of itself and is never edited by hand; `e2e/` holds the one end-to-end test |

## Working agreements (interview, 2026-09-16)

* **ADR-gated cadence.** An agent drafts the ADR and spec first; Kent accepts, rejects, or amends; only then is code written. Nothing is implemented against a `proposed` ADR. Decisions Kent has already taken are listed in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3 — do not re-litigate them.
* **Disgust veto.** Two conditions end a line of work immediately: a template-looking UI, and any state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule, or a cited source.
* **Vocabulary is the interface.** Use `spec/vocabulary.md` words exactly in docs, code, and UI copy.
* **Every number can say why.** Beliefs carry owner, interval, and provenance; two significant figures; model, user, and market beliefs are never merged.
* **Stacks tell the story.** One stack per spec; the bottom PR is docs-only; branch names are `<type>/<NN>-<slug>` with `NN` the stack number from the PRD roadmap. Conventional commits with `spec:` and `adr:` types in addition to the usual.
* **ARCHITECTURE.md is living.** A pull request that changes a boundary, layer, data flow, or runtime dependency updates it in the same PR.
* **Research reports are inputs.** Where a report and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins; where an ADR and the PRD disagree, fix the drift in the same PR.

RULES FOR THIS REPO

* Significant architectural decisions should be recorded at ./docs/adr in a numbered order. Higher number records supersede lower numbered ones.
* Enduring context between agents should live as all caps docs in the root of the repo, e.g. AGENTS.md, ASSIGNMENT.md, PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md. These should always be kept up to date if you notice them drifting.
* More detailed descriptions, diagrams about particular systems or complex features should be written to ./spec
* Specs should follow best practices regarding spec-driven development. Some key aspects of specs for this repo should include invariants and anti-patterns
* This is an experimental prototype and I am a solo developer. However, I would like to use best practices regarding commit messages, PRs, and PR stacks to maintain the navigability, hygiene, and legibility of this repo.
* Docs should avoid jargon, reference to other docs, or unexplained abbreviations and symbols. They should be self-contained as much as possible. That is, explain in doc what the concepts being referenced are. This also extends to doc strings and comments in the code.
* Be concise, punchy, and succinct without sacrificing clarity. Use formatting as a communication and legibility aid.

59	## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against
60	
61	Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.
62	
63	```python
64	class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
65	    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
66	    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
67	    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
68	    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
69	    # mode, the recording date and the prompt hash are on Receipt and nowhere else (S3)
70	
71	class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
72	    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
73	    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
74	    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
75	    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand
76	
77	class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
78	    at: int
79	    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
80	    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences
81	
82	class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
83	    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate
84	
85	class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
86	    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
87	    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
88	    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
89	    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
90	    why: str                            # one plain sentence
91	
92	class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
93	    model: str
94	    calls: int
95	    input_tokens: int
96	    output_tokens: int
97	    cache_read_tokens: int
98	    dollars: float
99	    seconds: float
100	    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
101	    recording_date: date | None
102	    prompt_hash: str
103	
104	class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
105	    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap", "claim_cap",
106	                    "search_cap", "spend_cap", "model_stopped", "no_terminal"]
107	                                        # why the GENERATION stopped. "no_path" is on Verdict only (S3)
108	    claims: int
109	    links: int
110	    rejected: int
111	
112	class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
113	    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
114	```
115	
116	**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.
117	
118	**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except two (S4)**: `receipt` is **rebuilt** with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash; and `beliefs_propagated` is **recomputed** — the recording carries the seed, `domain/` re-propagates, and **a recording therefore holds no `World` at all**, which keeps the file small and makes replay and live agree by construction. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.
119

122	## 04a pull request 0 — the engine fix both stacks stand on (G2, G3)
123	
124	**What is wrong, measured** (Hormuz, seed 20261001, `Observe(target="B", value=True)`, the shipped 2 000 versions × 8 worlds; re-run by the coordinator on 2026-09-17): **209 of the 2 000 versions have no surviving world.** Such a version reports `0.0` (`domain/propagation.py`, `_per_version`) and counts for nothing in the number and the band, because its weight is zero (`_draw`). But `_agreement_on` in `domain/diff.py` takes a plain unweighted mean of the signs, so each dead version **votes against the direction**. M1 and M2 both read 89.05% against the 90% bar, both read `unchanged`, the rail is empty, and **This happened** looks like a button that does nothing. Counted with the weights: **98.66%** (99.44% among survivors).
125	
126	**The rule (Kent, G2): read the direction with the same weights the number was read with.** `_agreement_on` takes the version weights; its two callers, `_states` and `_ranked_endings`, already hold them. Under the five edits that are not an observation every weight is 1, so not one bit moves anywhere else — **pin that with a test that compares a non-observe diff with itself before and after the change, never with a typed-in number.** Worlds per version stays 8. The 90% bar is untouched.
127	
128	**A claim moved only by reweighting (Kent, G3).** Observing C moves H from `.356` to `.365`, nearly twice the 0.005 floor, and H's same-direction share is zero **by construction**: H has no causes, so inside every version its answer is its own prior in both worlds and the paired difference is exactly zero. The diff states stay as they are. The diff's row for such a claim gains **one field** saying so (the agent names it from `spec/vocabulary.md`'s words and says why), and the Inspector prints one sentence, word for word: ***"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."*** The same shape as K4 — a fact about the reading lives in the Inspector.
129	
130	**In this pull request:** the dated amendment to record 0014 (dated in place, as record 0008 was — nothing in the decision changed; say what was measured and the one rule); `spec/multiverse/diff.md` open question 7 closed in place, the rule stated once, the reweighting paragraph added, and **every same-direction percentage the chapter quotes re-measured from the engine** (list which moved); `domain/diff.py`; tests `test_an_observation_puts_a_row_on_the_rail` · `test_a_dead_version_does_not_vote` · `test_direction_is_read_with_the_numbers_own_weights` · `test_an_edit_that_is_not_an_observation_is_unchanged_by_the_weights` · `test_a_claim_moved_only_by_reweighting_says_so`; `make types` and the regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`. `mypy --strict` clean, `domain/` stays at 100%.

There is no spinner anywhere, and a skeleton tile is on screen before the first model call returns — which is what NFR-7's "first paint within a second" actually means here, because one proposal takes seconds to come back (record 0006). Say so; NFR-7's words "of the first token" do not fit a pipeline that returns whole proposals, and the chapter corrects them.

144	- **A rejected proposal is shown, not hidden** — a short strip beside the map, one line per refusal, with the validator's own sentence. Watching the validator refuse the model is half the product (record 0012).

149	
150	**Four questions closed in place, each in the chapter that owns it.** `diff-view.md` open question 1 — the retraction badge now comes **from the world**, not from the branch, because the world carries `retractions` and two derivations of one line will eventually disagree. `inspector.md` open question 2 — the receipt and the transcript live in the panel's own section, fed by the `receipt` event. `inspector.md` open question 3 — the panel now shows the full decomposition, so the half block goes away. `diff.md` open question 5 — a terminal that did not move renders as a greyed row reading *no change*, because silence cannot be told from absence.
151	
152	---

154	## 04a pull request 2 — the join
155	
156	`frontend/src/world/apiSource.ts` stops throwing. Three calls, all already answering on `main`:
157	
158	```ts
159	readWorld({ baseId, branch, seed })       // POST /api/worlds        -> World
160	readDiff({ baseId, branchA, branchB, seed })  // POST /api/worlds/diff   -> Diff
161	readConditional({ baseId, branch, seed, linkId })  // POST /api/worlds/conditional -> Belief
162	```
163	
164	`App.tsx` hands the canvas an `ApiWorldSource`; `FixtureWorldSource` **stays**, and the app falls back to it when the world route fails, saying so — a map you can still read beats a blank screen.
165	
166	**What fills in, and nothing is deleted** (stack 03b shipped absences, never falsehoods):
167	
168	| Slot that read as an absence | What it now reads |
169	|---|---|
170	| Every model chip | `.35 (.20–.49)`, two significant figures with the certainty guard (`>.99`, `<.01`) |
171	| `WorldView.versions` | Present, so the chip switches to record 0014's **computed** sentence rather than the *stated* one (Kent's K3) |
172	| `pathProduct` | The multiplied-out likelihood of the best-backed route (INV-8) |
173	| A wire's midpoint chip | Fetched lazily on hover or selection, cached per `(branch, seed, link)`; still the **supposed** number, never the observed one |
174	| The delta rail | The engine's ranked rows, in the engine's order, with the two columns headed **how firm** and **same direction** |
175	| A tile's diff state | The fifth state, `shifted`, with before → after and a directional chevron |
176	| The retraction badge | From `World.retractions` |
177	
178	**The reweighting sentence (G3).** When the engine's diff row says a claim moved only by reweighting, the Inspector prints, word for word, *"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."* The field comes from the regenerated types in 04a pull request 0; the browser never works it out for itself.
179	
180	**The six buttons now move numbers.** Each appends an edit to the branch and asks for a new world and a new diff. **Split this claim** stays visibly not live (stack 06). **Add a claim** now needs the model and is 04a pull request 3's `POST /api/generate/insert`; until that lands it says so.
181	
182	**The browser's structural states become a hint.** The engine's affected set is the authority. A component test pins the browser's four structural states against the engine's `Diff` on the Hormuz strike branch, and a disagreement fails the build.

# Stack 04 — generation (04a ∥ 04b)

**Nothing is waiting on Kent. He answered everything on 2026-09-17** — six questions and eight small corrections, after a read-only design review. The answers are in **`plans/notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`** (rows G1–G6 and S1–S8), they are binding, and this plan has been rewritten in place to match them. In one breath: **no ensemble** — the model's stated range, labelled (record 0015, G1); **"This happened" is fixed by counting only the versions that survived** (G2), and a claim moved only by reweighting says so in the Inspector (G3); **up to three silent retries after a refusal** (G4); **$500 for the stack, a $15 hard stop per run in code, and only the coordinator spends money** (G5); **Hormuz recorded early, all four once the prompt is frozen** (G6).

---

**Goal:** type any sentence and watch a real map build itself, one claim at a time, with evidence — and with no key, watch the same thing play from a recording. After this stack the four example hypotheses from `ASSIGNMENT.md` all open, the numbers on screen are the engine's, and every proposal the validator refused is visible on the way past.

**What this stack must not do.** No thesis card, no stop-loss, no tail strip, no live market prices (stack 05). No storage — nothing is kept between requests except what a running process holds in memory; the SQLite file is stack 05's (FR-31). No `refine`, no probes, no feedback-arrow unrolling (stack 06). **No re-prompting for a whole map**, ever (anti-pattern 2). **The model never mints an identifier, never declares its own provenance, and never decides whether a map is legal** (anti-pattern 1, record 0003). No ensemble and no graph-to-graph reconciliation — record 0015 (Kent, G1). No pastcast (FR-30, stack 07).

**Rests on:** record **0006** (the model boundary — the SDK, the model, structured output, one proposal per call, the web-search tool, the cached system prompt, refusals shown not hidden), **0008** (five testing layers; recorded responses; evals out of band), **0012** (replay mode, accepted 2026-09-17 — built here), **0003** (the model proposes, our code disposes), **0014** (what it defers to 04: the provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, and the open question that became record 0015, accepted 2026-09-17), **0005** (link semantics), **0010** (grounding; mostly stack 05, but FR-28's search at generation time is here). Read each record's "Decision Outcome" before writing a line.

> ### Before any code that calls Claude, load the `claude-api` skill.
> Model names, request shapes, parameter names and prices change, and memory is unreliable. **Record 0006 holds the verified specifics** — the client library, the model name, the structured-output call, the thinking setting, the server-side web-search tool name, the cache-control block, the refusal stop reason. **Verify every one of them against the skill before typing it**, and put the price table in exactly one module with the date it was read beside it. This plan deliberately contains no model name, no parameter and no dollar figure. Every agent's brief carries this paragraph.

---

## How 04a and 04b stay out of each other's way

Two stacks, in parallel, as 03a ∥ 03b ran. **04a is the browser; 04b is the server.** The split of every file that could collide:

| File or tree | Owner this cycle | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src/**` except `api/schema.ts` | **04a** | 04b never edits a component, a hook or a stylesheet |
| `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` | **04b** | Only 04b runs `make types`, once, in its top pull request. A `schema.ts` diff on a 04a branch is a mistake to revert — **with one exception: 04a's bottom pull request, the engine fix (agent F), regenerates it for the one new field on a diff row** |
| `backend/**`, `evals/**`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.env.example` | **04b** | 04a never edits a Python file — **except agent F, in 04a's bottom pull request, which owns `domain/diff.py` and its tests for that pull request only** |
| `spec/workbench/**` | **04a** | Including the new `streaming-growth.md` |
| `spec/generation/**`, `docs/adr/**` | **04b** | |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | **04b**, in its top pull request only | 04b's agent writes the browser sentences from 04a's merged state, so **04a merges first** |

**04a's first three pull requests merge first** (the fix, the chapter, the join). They need nothing from 04b to be correct, and they unblock Kent's eye on real computed numbers days before the model pipeline exists. **04a's last pull request — the growing canvas — is held until 04b's stream pull request is on `main`** (S6): its browser test plays a recording through a route 04b owns, **Add a claim** calls 04b's `POST /api/generate/insert`, and the `e2e` job runs every spec, so merging it early turns `main` red. When 04b's top pull request is ready, rebase its branch onto the finished `main` rather than merging `main` into it — a linear child restacks itself (STATUS, 2026-09-17).

**The one true dependency:** 04a's third pull request draws a map as it streams, and the stream is 04b's. It is handled three ways and no other. (i) **The event vocabulary is settled in this plan**, below, and pasted into both stacks' briefs — the shapes-sheet trick from stack 02. (ii) 04a types the events by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`, exactly as stack 03b hand-typed `WorldView`; 04b's top pull request regenerates `schema.ts` and adds a **type-level test** that fails if the two drift. (iii) The 04a growth agent is launched in wave 2, after 04b's stream route is green on its branch, and develops against a server run out of the 04b worktree — read-only, no edits, no shared files.

## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against

Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.

```python
class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
    # mode, the recording date and the prompt hash are on Receipt and nowhere else (S3)

class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand

class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
    at: int
    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences

class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate

class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
    why: str                            # one plain sentence

class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
    model: str
    calls: int
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    dollars: float
    seconds: float
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    recording_date: date | None
    prompt_hash: str

class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap", "claim_cap",
                    "search_cap", "spend_cap", "model_stopped", "no_terminal"]
                                        # why the GENERATION stopped. "no_path" is on Verdict only (S3)
    claims: int
    links: int
    rejected: int

class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
```

**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.

**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except two (S4)**: `receipt` is **rebuilt** with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash; and `beliefs_propagated` is **recomputed** — the recording carries the seed, `domain/` re-propagates, and **a recording therefore holds no `World` at all**, which keeps the file small and makes replay and live agree by construction. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

## 04b pull request 2 — the pipeline

```python
# engine/proposal.py — what the model is allowed to return. One of three.
class ClaimProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["claim"]
    claim: str                       # the sentence, as a person would say it
    claim_kind: Literal["event", "market", "not_tradeable"]
    resolution: Resolution           # criteria, judge, resolve-by (INV-1)
    prior: Ranged                    # p, lo, hi. No owner field: we stamp "model"
    base_rate: BaseRate | None
    payoff: ContractPayoff | PricePayoff | None   # required when claim_kind == "market"
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None              # required when claim_kind == "not_tradeable"
    cause: str                       # the identifier of a claim ALREADY on the map
    link: LinkDraft                  # the arrow from that cause into this new claim

class LinkProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["link"]
    source: str                      # both ends already on the map
    target: str
    link: LinkDraft

class Stop(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["stop"]
    why: str                         # one sentence, shown in the transcript

class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    strength: float
    lag: int
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]
    half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...] # NO provenance field, and no identifier field

Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]
```

**Three things the model is structurally unable to do**, because the fields do not exist: mint an identifier, declare its own provenance, and return more than one thing. A new claim's identifier is minted by `engine/ids.py`; an existing claim is named by an identifier the prompt handed it; `owner="model"` is stamped by us; and **provenance is decided by us from what actually happened** — at least one cited source **that the search tool itself returned in that call** → `documented` (S1: a URL the model typed that the tool never returned is not a source, and is dropped with a note in the transcript); a rationale with no such source → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` come from stack 05's adapters and never from a proposal.

```python
# engine/expand.py
def expand(graph: Graph, frontier: PropositionId, *, target: str | None) -> Outcome
```

One call, one proposal, then `domain.validate` on the map the proposal would leave behind. Accepted → mint, emit `proposal_accepted`. Rejected → emit `proposal_rejected` with **every** violation, and never repair. Both are events; both go in the transcript. **After a refusal the engine asks again for the same frontier claim, up to three times in a row, and the next call is never told what was wrong (Kent, G4)** — violation text never enters a prompt.

**The caps, all arguments with these defaults** (*decided here*): depth 5 layers · width 3 children per claim · 30 claims in total · 3 refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim · 3 frontier claims expanded concurrently · **a cap on web searches per generation (S2; the agent picks the default and justifies it in `proposals.md`)** · **a spending cap per run, default $15 (G5)**. Record 0006 *estimates* a 30-claim map at about 40 calls; the first real measurement goes in `STATUS.md`.

**Two stop rules that are not caps.** A generation ends at `reached_terminal` when every open frontier claim has closed and the map has at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9). If the caps are hit with no ending at all, the engine makes **one last call per open claim asking only for an ending** — and if that still fails, the stream ends `no_terminal` and the browser says so honestly. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose.

**The Verify door.** The destination is added to the map up front as an ordinary claim; every call is told what it is; expansion is steered toward it. `no_path` is returned when the caps are hit and no path from the hypothesis reaches it, naming the nearest claim that was reached. **A bridge is never invented** — there is no code path that adds an arrow to make a path exist, and the eval case whose destination is unreachable proves it.

**Cost, and the hard stop (G5).** `engine/receipt.py` folds every call's usage into one `Receipt`, **and the pipeline checks the running receipt against the run's spending cap after every call**: over the cap, the generation ends `done.reason = "spend_cap"` with a plain sentence naming what was spent and what was got. The cap across runs ($500 for the stack) is a working agreement kept in `STATUS.md` — nothing is stored between runs until stack 05. **Only the coordinator runs a command that spends money; no sub-agent ever holds the key.** The pipeline agent builds against hand-written fake responses, adds `make record-cassettes`, and stops; the coordinator records. `engine/pricing.py` holds the price table and **nothing else**, with the day it was read and the `claude-api` skill named in a comment. A run whose cache reads stay at zero is a bug, not a slow day.

**Tests** — `backend/tests/boundary/test_expand_cassettes.py`, recordings in `backend/tests/cassettes/`, `@pytest.mark.vcr`, the suite already runs `--record-mode=none` so an unrecorded call fails rather than dialling out. **Every model call goes to one URL, so the recorder must match on the request body as well** (or the boundary tests run one call at a time) — otherwise two calls in flight are handed each other's answers:

| `POST /api/generate/insert` | `{base_id, branch, claim_in_words, at}` | One `Insert` intervention — a claim and its arrows, drafted and validated — for the browser to append to its branch |

**`insert` is the one intervention that calls the model** (anti-pattern 2's single exception: re-prompt only for `insert`, and only over the affected subtree). The other five stay pure arithmetic in `domain/`, so a reviewer with no key still gets the whole multiverse at full fidelity.

**Where a transcript lives before stack 05's SQLite** (*decided here*): in memory, keyed by generation identifier, for the life of the process, and streamed to the browser as it is produced. Nothing is written to disk except by `make record-demo`. Writing a second on-disk store now would be a store we have to migrate in stack 05 for no gain today.

**The stream is a plain `StreamingResponse` generator (S5).** No `sse-starlette`: one fewer dependency, and no heartbeat comment line to land in a recording. The generator writes `event:` and `data:` lines itself, and stops calling the model when the client goes away — a test pins that. **`versions` and `worlds` get upper bounds on this route and on the three world routes (S2)**; today they are bounded below only.

**Replay** (record 0012), in `engine/replay.py`: no key → the four examples play from `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl` through this same route (**Hormuz is recorded as soon as the pipeline runs; the other three once the prompt is frozen, at the end of this pull request — G6**), at a fixed cosmetic delay that an `instant` flag drops for tests. Beliefs are **not** replayed as numbers: the recording carries the seed and `domain/` re-propagates, so replay and live agree by construction (INV-5). Every recording carries **at least one `proposal_rejected`** and **one recorded intervention** — the scripted "…but Iran is struck the next day" its card offers. Any other insert is declined in plain words: *"drafting a new claim needs a model key."*

`make record-demo` is the only way a recording is written, and a recording is remade whenever a prompt changes — the same checklist line the cassettes already carry. A sixth continuous-integration job, **`recordings`**, **passes on an empty folder** (so it is green from the commit that adds it), parses every file, checks each holds a refusal, and checks each prompt hash equals the current prompt's. **The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths** — settled by Kent in record 0014 and deferred to here because every arrow on the Hormuz fixture is hand-written `argued` or `asserted`, so doing it in 03a would have widened everything equally and taught nobody anything. Now generation produces arrows that genuinely differ.

```python
# domain/propagation.py
PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[str, float] = {
    "documented": 0.15, "historical": 0.15, "market_implied": 0.15,
    "argued": 0.40, "user": 0.40,
    "simulated": 0.50,
    "asserted": 0.60,
}
```

Each of the 2 000 versions draws every arrow's strength from a normal centred on the stated strength with that standard deviation, **on the same log-odds scale the strength is written in**. "How well-backed is this" becomes "how wide is this" with no extra elicitation. **There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, now or ever** — the spread is derived, never stored. The draw stream is **per arrow**, derived from the seed and a hash of the arrow's own identifier, exactly as the per-claim streams already are, so adding an arrow cannot shift another arrow's draws and version *k* of two worlds still shares its numbers.

**Three consequences, and the third is the one that bites.** `test_band_is_not_sampling_noise` must now freeze **both** priors and spreads to get a zero-width band — it gains a parameter. `test_range_matches_analytic_first_order_on_fixture` needs the strength terms in its delta method. ### The gates

**M4a** — the join: three pull requests open and green; the Hormuz map draws with the engine's own numbers; `shifted` renders; the rail ranks; the conditional fetches; the six buttons move numbers. Kent has looked at it and nothing triggered a veto.

**M4b** — generation: four pull requests open and green; typing a sentence grows a map tile by tile with evidence and visible refusals; Verify grades a path or says there is none; with no key all four examples replay through the same stream; `make eval` prints a scorecard; the cost of a map is written down.

1	# Kent's decisions on stack 03's open design questions — 2026-09-17, second round
2	
3	Asked through the question tool after an Opus design review of every open question in pull requests #18, #19, #21 and the canvas branch. Kent took the recommended option on all eleven and approved the fourteen small ones as a block. **All of these are settled. Reopen nothing.** Each is marked below with where it lands.
4	
5	## The eleven
6	
7	| # | Topic | Decision (Kent, 2026-09-17) | Lands in |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| K1 | **Feedback arrows** | **One named rule, written once in `spec/multiverse/interventions.md`:** *the map the engine works through is the map with feedback (reflexive) arrows set aside. Anything that asks "what can move" reads that map — the affected set, diff states, propagation's ordering, layering. Anything that asks "what can I walk to" reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline.* Every other chapter cites it instead of re-deciding. A named test, `test_a_feedback_arrow_never_carries_a_change`, fails loudly the day stack 06 unrolls them and points at the one sentence to change. R is `untouched` on the strike branch | `interventions.md`; cited by `propagation.md`, `diff.md`, `diff-view.md`, `layout-and-zoom.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md`; `domain/patch.py` `affected_set`; tests |
10	| K2 | **Rounding** | **Two significant figures on the number AND both range ends, plus a certainty guard: a chip never prints `1.0` or `.0` — it prints `>.99` and `<.01`.** `.06` prints `.060`. NFR-1's example becomes `.35 (.22–.50)`; `belief.md` §B3's example likewise, and its open question 5 closes | PRD NFR-1; `belief.md`; `keyboard-and-access.md` B6; `BeliefChip.tsx` + test |
11	| K3 | **The chip's hover sentence** | **Two sentences, picked by whether a world computed anything.** `WorldView` gains one optional field, `versions`. Present → record 0014's label and sentence, word for word. Absent → the *stated* sentence the Inspector already uses under PRIOR: "this range is stated, not computed — it says how sure the elicitation was." No new copy; chip and Inspector share the two sentences so they cannot drift | `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `inspector.md`, `diff-view.md` (`WorldView`); `world/types.ts`, `BeliefChip.tsx` + test |
12	| K4 | **`killed`** | **Forced false, full stop.** "No path left from the hypothesis" stops being a diff state; it is a fact about the *path*, reported by the Inspector's path bar: "no path from the hypothesis reaches this claim any more." | `diff.md`, `vocabulary.md`, `diff-view.md`, `inspector.md`; `domain/diff.py`; the canvas's structural `killed` |
13	| K5 | **The rank's path; "how firm"** | **Path = the best-backed route** — over every path from *any* differing edit's subject to the terminal, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest (widest bottleneck; a ten-line Dijkstra variant), read over **the same graph the affected set is computed over**. "Shortest" and "which subject" both disappear. **`range_width` = the width of world B's own band on that claim at `at_day`** — the same quantity the tile shows. On Hormuz nothing changes: M1 0.6, N1 0.3 | `diff.md`; `domain/diff.py`; `diff-view.md`; the path bar uses the same path |
14	| K6 | **A fourth refusal code** | **`edit_not_applicable`** — "this edit cannot be folded onto this map as written". Covers `refine` (not built), an `insert` whose arrow touches neither end of the new claim, and a branch chain that loops or names a missing branch. `unknown_target` goes back to meaning exactly what it says | `domain/validity.py`, `domain/patch.py`, tests; `interventions.md` OQ5, `branches-and-worlds.md` OQ3, `validity.md` |
15	| K7 | **Where "no market" gets its reason** | **The tile says `no market` and nothing else.** The reason moves to the Inspector and the chip's hover/accessible name, written once in `spec/vocabulary.md` and chosen by `kind`: a `market` claim — "no venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff"; an `event` or `hypothesis` — "no venue quotes this claim"; a `not_tradeable` ending keeps **its own stored reason on the tile**, because that one is a finding | `vocabulary.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `inspector.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md`; `Tile.tsx`, `fixtureSource.ts` |
16	| K8 | **Zoom** | **Derived, not chosen:** summary tiles below `11/13 ≈ 0.85`; zoom floor `11/22 = 0.5`. Both are consequences of "text never below 11 pixels". No counter-scaling. Supersedes the plan's 0.6 | `layout-and-zoom.md`; `graph/geometry.ts` (already done) |
17	| K9 | **Tile height** | **Content-fit, clamped 152–272 px, on the 8-px grid, computed from the content** (never measured from the screen, so layout stays a pure function). The chapter's "96–216" is corrected | `tiles-ports-wires.md`; `geometry.ts` (already done) |
18	| K10 | **The rail's column heading** | On screen the column reads **"same direction"**. The field stays `agreement`. The word *agreement* on screen is left free for stack 04's run-to-run number. The other column reads **"how firm"** | `vocabulary.md`, `diff-view.md`, `diff.md` (one line) |
19	| K11 | **Chip layout** | **Stacked, as built:** owner, the number, the range beneath. The one-line form `.61 (.45–.74)` stays for prose, the outline and the accessible name | `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md` |
20	
21	## The fourteen small ones — approved as a block ("Yes, take all 14")
22	
23	| Question | Decision | Why |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| FR-21 / record 0014 say "its own base rate" | Amend both, dated, to "its own **prior**" | B has no base rate; what varies between versions is `prior`. A factual repair |
26	| Union layout slides every base claim one column right | Following focus is enough, plus: **creating a claim moves focus to it**, so `setCenter` frames the strike. Do not pin columns | The shift is a rigid translation; pinning would put a cause to the right of its effect |
27	| `h`/`l` among several wires | Nearest on the cross-axis; the others become the `j`/`k` set where you land. The status line names the wire taken | Two keystrokes reach any neighbour; a chooser overlay is a pop-up in all but name |
28	| Which path the path-product bar shows | The same best-backed path the ranking uses (K5); the bar names its steps | One path-choosing rule, used twice |
29	| "+n more" | First seven in the layout's own within-column order; activating "+n more" opens the **outline view** filtered to that column | Reuses two things that exist and are deterministic |
30	| `apply` and a failing edit | Stop at the first edit that does not fit; report **every** violation that edit produced | Later edits may name things the failed edit would have added |
31	| `observe` carries no date | Leave it; close `interventions.md` OQ3: you can only observe the past, and the window starts today, so `at = None` ⇒ day zero is exactly right | `Do` needs a date because a supposition can be about the future |
32	| An `impulse` with no `half_life` | A new violation code, **`impulse_without_half_life`**, checked by `validate`. Reject, never repair | The mirror of `half_life_without_impulse` (#16): the shape and its parameters must agree, checked both ways |
33	| A `ramp` with `lag = 0.0` | Nothing to decide: evaluate the `u ≥ L` branch first and the rise branch is empty. One sentence says a zero-lag ramp behaves as a step, as a *consequence* | No division by zero, no special case |

# Kent's decisions on stack 03's open design questions — 2026-09-17, second round

Asked through the question tool after an Opus design review of every open question in pull requests #18, #19, #21 and the canvas branch. Kent took the recommended option on all eleven and approved the fourteen small ones as a block. **All of these are settled. Reopen nothing.** Each is marked below with where it lands.

## The eleven

| # | Topic | Decision (Kent, 2026-09-17) | Lands in |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | **Feedback arrows** | **One named rule, written once in `spec/multiverse/interventions.md`:** *the map the engine works through is the map with feedback (reflexive) arrows set aside. Anything that asks "what can move" reads that map — the affected set, diff states, propagation's ordering, layering. Anything that asks "what can I walk to" reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline.* Every other chapter cites it instead of re-deciding. A named test, `test_a_feedback_arrow_never_carries_a_change`, fails loudly the day stack 06 unrolls them and points at the one sentence to change. R is `untouched` on the strike branch | `interventions.md`; cited by `propagation.md`, `diff.md`, `diff-view.md`, `layout-and-zoom.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md`; `domain/patch.py` `affected_set`; tests |
| K2 | **Rounding** | **Two significant figures on the number AND both range ends, plus a certainty guard: a chip never prints `1.0` or `.0` — it prints `>.99` and `<.01`.** `.06` prints `.060`. NFR-1's example becomes `.35 (.22–.50)`; `belief.md` §B3's example likewise, and its open question 5 closes | PRD NFR-1; `belief.md`; `keyboard-and-access.md` B6; `BeliefChip.tsx` + test |
| K3 | **The chip's hover sentence** | **Two sentences, picked by whether a world computed anything.** `WorldView` gains one optional field, `versions`. Present → record 0014's label and sentence, word for word. Absent → the *stated* sentence the Inspector already uses under PRIOR: "this range is stated, not computed — it says how sure the elicitation was." No new copy; chip and Inspector share the two sentences so they cannot drift | `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `inspector.md`, `diff-view.md` (`WorldView`); `world/types.ts`, `BeliefChip.tsx` + test |
| K4 | **`killed`** | **Forced false, full stop.** "No path left from the hypothesis" stops being a diff state; it is a fact about the *path*, reported by the Inspector's path bar: "no path from the hypothesis reaches this claim any more." | `diff.md`, `vocabulary.md`, `diff-view.md`, `inspector.md`; `domain/diff.py`; the canvas's structural `killed` |
| K5 | **The rank's path; "how firm"** | **Path = the best-backed route** — over every path from *any* differing edit's subject to the terminal, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest (widest bottleneck; a ten-line Dijkstra variant), read over **the same graph the affected set is computed over**. "Shortest" and "which subject" both disappear. **`range_width` = the width of world B's own band on that claim at `at_day`** — the same quantity the tile shows. On Hormuz nothing changes: M1 0.6, N1 0.3 | `diff.md`; `domain/diff.py`; `diff-view.md`; the path bar uses the same path |
| K6 | **A fourth refusal code** | **`edit_not_applicable`** — "this edit cannot be folded onto this map as written". Covers `refine` (not built), an `insert` whose arrow touches neither end of the new claim, and a branch chain that loops or names a missing branch. `unknown_target` goes back to meaning exactly what it says | `domain/validity.py`, `domain/patch.py`, tests; `interventions.md` OQ5, `branches-and-worlds.md` OQ3, `validity.md` |
| K7 | **Where "no market" gets its reason** | **The tile says `no market` and nothing else.** The reason moves to the Inspector and the chip's hover/accessible name, written once in `spec/vocabulary.md` and chosen by `kind`: a `market` claim — "no venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff"; an `event` or `hypothesis` — "no venue quotes this claim"; a `not_tradeable` ending keeps **its own stored reason on the tile**, because that one is a finding | `vocabulary.md`, `tiles-ports-wires.md`, `inspector.md`, `keyboard-and-access.md`; `Tile.tsx`, `fixtureSource.ts` |

| A `ramp` with `lag = 0.0` | Nothing to decide: evaluate the `u ≥ L` branch first and the rise branch is empty. One sentence says a zero-lag ramp behaves as a step, as a *consequence* | No division by zero, no special case |

A second supposition can still be undermined by a *new* arrow added after it. A consequence of the settled rule, not a change to it | Falls out of "a later assignment overrides an earlier one" |

| Five strength-word bands or `link.md`'s four anchors | Five bands: the four anchors with the gaps filled and one band below 0.25. Say so in `link.md`; close both questions | A refinement, not a conflict |
| Stacked chips | (Became K11) | — |
