1	# Vocabulary
2	
3	Every document, identifier, and UI label uses these words exactly. If a better word appears, change it here first and then everywhere else (L2.21: understanding enables composition; shared words are the interface).
4	
5	## Propositions and links
6	
7	**Hypothesis.** The user's root input. A proposition asserted by `do()`, carrying the user's prior as a `user` belief. There is exactly one per graph.
8	
9	**Proposition.** A node. A *resolvable* claim — something that will be true or false by a date, judged by a named source. Never a vibe ("tensions ease"); always a check ("≥14 consecutive days of unrestricted commercial transit per Lloyd's List by 2026-11-01").
10	- `kind`: `hypothesis` · `event` · `market` (terminal; names an instrument) · `not_tradeable` (terminal; names the reason).
11	- `resolution`: `{criteria, source, by}` — all required (INV-1).
12	- `prior`: the model's marginal belief before parents are considered.
13	- `base_rate` (optional): `{reference_class, k, n, sources}`.
14	- `evidence[]`: `{claim, url, direction ∈ {+1, −1}, weight}`.
15	- `payoff` (market only): one of two shapes, told apart by a `kind` field. A **contract payoff** — `kind: contract` — names a venue, the venue's own identifier for the contract, its title, and the side you would take (`yes` or `no`). A **price payoff** — `kind: price` — names an instrument, a direction (`long` or `short`), and `move`, how far the price is expected to move if the claim comes out true, as a fraction (0.03 is three per cent). The rule behind both: the domain names *what you would trade*; what it costs — price, spread, and when we looked — is a market belief, fetched live.
16	
17	**Link.** An edge. A causal claim from one proposition to another.
18	- `mode`: `trigger` — horizontal/sequential causality (dominoes): fires once when the parent becomes true, effect persists and decays; removing the parent later does not undo it. `sustain` — vertical causality (the desk holds the apple): the effect exists only while the parent holds; removing the parent retracts the effect.
19	- `strength`: how much the link shifts the child's odds while active, on a log-odds scale (so several links add up instead of multiplying).
20	- `lag`: time from parent-true to link-active. `shape`: `impulse` (a one-time spike that fades with `half_life`) · `step` (switches on and holds) · `ramp` (builds up over `lag`).
21	- `rationale`: the mechanism in one to three sentences. `sources[]`. There is no field for how sure the model is about its own mechanism; `provenance` and the rationale carry that.
22	- `provenance`: see below. `reflexive`: market → world feedback; requires `lag > 0` (INV-6).
23	
24	**Provenance.** Where a number or link came from. `asserted` (model, no evidence) · `argued` (model, mechanism stated) · `documented` (cited sources) · `market_implied` (a live price) · `historical` (event study) · `user` · `simulated` (a probe). Encoded on every chip and wire (INV-2, INV-12).
25	
26	**Belief.** `{p, lo, hi, owner}` with `owner ∈ {model, user, market}` and `0 ≤ lo ≤ p ≤ hi ≤ 1` (INV-7). The three owners are stored and rendered separately and never averaged (INV-11). Rendered at two significant figures with the interval. `lo` and `hi` are the 10th and 90th percentiles of the likelihood itself — how sure we are of the number, not how much the world can move.
27	
28	**Graph.** Propositions + links. A DAG after removing `reflexive` links; reflexive links unroll in time (INV-6). Has exactly one hypothesis and ≥1 terminal (INV-9). Immutable once created; changes are branches.
29	
30	## The multiverse
31	
32	**Intervention.** One operation on a graph:
33	- `do(n, value, at?)` — assert. Cuts the incoming links `n` has **at the moment the edit is applied**; a link inserted later is live. A timed assertion — `do(H, at=Oct 1)` says H holds from the 1st, not that H is sealed for ever. Ancestors unchanged (INV-3). This is what a hypothesis is.
34	- `observe(n, value)` — learn. Updates ancestors as well as descendants. Distinct verb in the UI.
35	- `insert(node, links[])` — "…but X happens." Adds a proposition and its links.
36	- `retune(link, strength)` — the user disagrees with a number.
37	- `refine(n → children[])` — split a proposition into finer sub-propositions; their combined likelihood must equal the original's (they *marginalize* back to `n`, INV-10). The brainstorm's "search deeper lines".
38	- `believe(n, belief)` — record the user's own belief on `n`. Lives in the branch so it replays and diffs; never alters `model` or `market` beliefs; not propagated in v1 (D8, INV-11). Propagating a user's world is a stretch (see `probes/`).
39	
40	**Branch.** A named, ordered list of interventions over a base graph. A branch *is* a patch. Branches compose by concatenation; `apply(g, [])` is `g` (INV-5). Branches may have a parent branch.
41	
42	**World.** A base graph with a branch applied and beliefs propagated. Replayable from `(base_id, branch, seed)` (INV-5, NFR-2). The base world is the empty branch.
43	
44	**Diff.** Between two worlds: per proposition, `unchanged` · `shifted` (with before → after) · `added` · `killed`; plus a ranked list of terminal deltas and a one-line natural-language summary. **`killed` means forced false, and nothing else** (decided 2026-09-17) — never "its number got small", and never "no path reaches it from the hypothesis any more", which is a fact about the *path* and is reported by the Inspector's path bar in those words. The ranking is the size of the move times the weakest provenance weight on the **best-backed route** from a differing edit's subject to that ending: over every such route, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest. Two factors; range width and agreement are columns beside it and are never multiplied in.
45	
46	**Version of the map.** One coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind: every claim's likelihood drawn from its own stated range at once, never every low end together. The engine runs two thousand versions and eight worlds under each. The range on a computed number is the spread across versions; a change is read version by version, never by whether two ranges overlap.
47	
48	**Agreement.** The share of versions of the map in which a change moved the same way. Computed, never self-reported. A claim counts as `shifted` when it moved by .005 or more **and** agreement is at least 90%; agreement is then shown as its own column beside the change, never multiplied into the ranking. **On screen that column is headed *same direction*** (decided 2026-09-17), and the width column beside it is headed *how firm*; the field names stay `agreement` and `range_width`. Keeping the word *agreement* off this screen leaves it free for stack 04's run-to-run number. Stack 04 may compute a second agreement number — how far several independent generation runs agreed on a claim's likelihood (decision record 0014 defers that question). Same idea, same rule; wherever both could be meant, say which.
49	
50	**Locality.** An intervention changes only what is still connected to its subject in the graph the edit leaves behind (INV-4). Which claims those are depends on the operation, because the operations leave behind different graphs: `do` cuts the target's incoming arrows, so only the target and its descendants remain connected to it; `observe` cuts nothing, so its ancestors — and what those ancestors cause — are connected too. The per-operation **affected set** table in `multiverse/interventions.md` is the operational form, and the property test computes the set from the shape of the graph. The product's central correctness claim.
51	
52	## Sensitivity and drill-down
53	
54	**Sensitivity sweep.** One-at-a-time flip of every proposition; record Δ on each terminal.
55	
56	**Invalidation.** The proposition whose flip most damages a terminal *and* resolves before it *and* is publicly observable (INV-14). This is the stop-loss. **Take-profit** is the symmetric case. **Unhedgeable**: sensitive but not observable in time; listed, never used as a stop.
57	
58	**Tail.** A low-probability, high-magnitude proposition. Listed in its own strip with a suggested hedge; never averaged into an expected value.
59	
60	**Probe** (stretch). A modeling resource attached to one proposition: `monte_carlo` · `bayes_subnet` · `persona_redteam`. Output re-enters the graph as a `simulated` belief with its own rationale.
61	
62	**Value of information.** How much the trade depends on a proposition × how uncertain it is; ranks where a probe is worth its cost.
63	
64	## The finale
65	
66	**Thesis.** The compiled trade: `hypothesis`, `horizon`, `legs[]` (instrument, direction, size, driving proposition, model p, market p, edge), `entry`, `invalidation`, `take_profit`, `distribution` (p10/p50/p90, CVaR₅, max drawdown, P(ruin)), `tails[]`, `caveats` (weakest links, unhedgeable, crowding).
67	
68	**Strategy export.** A declarative JSON rendering of a thesis with graph references justifying each leg; the shape a downstream trading agent could ingest.
69	
70	## Surfaces
71	
72	**Workbench.** The main screen: canvas + world-state strip + Inspector + tail strip + thesis dock.
73	**Tile.** A proposition's on-canvas card. **Port.** A typed input/output on a tile. **Wire.** A link's on-canvas rendering. **Inspector.** The persistent side panel; never a modal. **Delta rail.** The ranked terminal-delta list beside a diff; its two side columns are headed **how firm** (the width of the new number's range) and **same direction** (the share of versions of the map that moved the same way — the field called `agreement`; on screen the word *agreement* is kept free for stack 04's run-to-run number). **Launchpad.** The empty state with the four seeded examples.
74	
75	## Interface words
76	
77	The six operations keep their code names in code, in the wire format and in this document — `do`, `observe`, `insert`, `retune`, `refine`, `believe` — and none of those words appears on screen. These are the words the user reads. Change a button here first, then everywhere else.
78	
79	| Code name | The button | The badge afterwards | What the interface says it means |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| `do` | **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** | "Take this as given, and do not tell me what caused it" |
82	| `observe` | **This happened** | **Happened · date** | "This is news — update what came before it too" |
83	| `insert` | **Add a claim**, hinted as "…but this also happens" | **Added** | A claim and its arrows arrive together |
84	| `retune` | **Change this push** | **Retuned** | "You moved this arrow from +0.7 to +0.3" |
85	| `refine` | **Split this claim** | **Split** | The finer claims add back up to the one they replace |
86	| `believe` | **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge | Your number sits beside the model's and the market's |
87	
88	One more badge is **derived**: no button produces it. **Retracted · date · by "…"** appears on a claim that was supposed true and has since been pushed back down by a later edit — what was holding this up was removed. It names the edit responsible and the day it landed (UX-14; the mechanism is in `multiverse/interventions.md`).
89	
90	## Words for a number that is not there
91	
92	An empty slot never shows a blank, a zero or a placeholder: it shows words and, one hover or one click away, a reason. These are the words; change them here first.
93	
94	| Where | On the tile | The reason, read in the Inspector and on the chip's hover |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| No market price, on a `market` claim | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff." |
97	| No market price, on an `event` or the `hypothesis` | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim." |
98	| No market price, on a `not_tradeable` ending | **no market**, with the claim's own stored reason **on the tile** — that reason is a finding, not boilerplate | the same stored reason |
99	| No number of your own yet | **—** and *add yours* | "You have not given a number for this claim." |
100	| Nothing has been computed | **no engine yet** | "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet." |
101	
102	## Words we do not use
103	
104	*Prediction* (we model arguments, not oracles) · *scenario* (ambiguous between branch and world) · *edge* when we mean a link (reserve *edge* for model-vs-market spread) · *node* in UI copy (say tile or proposition) · *confidence*, at all — there is no confidence field on anything. A link's standing is its `provenance` (a receipt we write), its rationale, and the range on the belief; a number for how much things computed independently agreed is called *agreement* — defined under *The multiverse* above — and is computed, never self-reported.

# Vocabulary

Every document, identifier, and UI label uses these words exactly. If a better word appears, change it here first and then everywhere else (L2.21: understanding enables composition; shared words are the interface).

## Propositions and links

**Hypothesis.** The user's root input. A proposition asserted by `do()`, carrying the user's prior as a `user` belief. There is exactly one per graph.

**Proposition.** A node. A *resolvable* claim — something that will be true or false by a date, judged by a named source. Never a vibe ("tensions ease"); always a check ("≥14 consecutive days of unrestricted commercial transit per Lloyd's List by 2026-11-01").
- `kind`: `hypothesis` · `event` · `market` (terminal; names an instrument) · `not_tradeable` (terminal; names the reason).
- `resolution`: `{criteria, source, by}` — all required (INV-1).
- `prior`: the model's marginal belief before parents are considered.
- `base_rate` (optional): `{reference_class, k, n, sources}`.
- `evidence[]`: `{claim, url, direction ∈ {+1, −1}, weight}`.
- `payoff` (market only): one of two shapes, told apart by a `kind` field. A **contract payoff** — `kind: contract` — names a venue, the venue's own identifier for the contract, its title, and the side you would take (`yes` or `no`). A **price payoff** — `kind: price` — names an instrument, a direction (`long` or `short`), and `move`, how far the price is expected to move if the claim comes out true, as a fraction (0.03 is three per cent). The rule behind both: the domain names *what you would trade*; what it costs — price, spread, and when we looked — is a market belief, fetched live.

**Link.** An edge. A causal claim from one proposition to another.
- `mode`: `trigger` — horizontal/sequential causality (dominoes): fires once when the parent becomes true, effect persists and decays; removing the parent later does not undo it. `sustain` — vertical causality (the desk holds the apple): the effect exists only while the parent holds; removing the parent retracts the effect.
- `strength`: how much the link shifts the child's odds while active, on a log-odds scale (so several links add up instead of multiplying).
- `lag`: time from parent-true to link-active. `shape`: `impulse` (a one-time spike that fades with `half_life`) · `step` (switches on and holds) · `ramp` (builds up over `lag`).
- `rationale`: the mechanism in one to three sentences. `sources[]`. There is no field for how sure the model is about its own mechanism; `provenance` and the rationale carry that.
- `provenance`: see below. `reflexive`: market → world feedback; requires `lag > 0` (INV-6).

**Provenance.** Where a number or link came from. `asserted` (model, no evidence) · `argued` (model, mechanism stated) · `documented` (cited sources) · `market_implied` (a live price) · `historical` (event study) · `user` · `simulated` (a probe). Encoded on every chip and wire (INV-2, INV-12).

**Belief.** `{p, lo, hi, owner}` with `owner ∈ {model, user, market}` and `0 ≤ lo ≤ p ≤ hi ≤ 1` (INV-7). The three owners are stored and rendered separately and never averaged (INV-11). Rendered at two significant figures with the interval. `lo` and `hi` are the 10th and 90th percentiles of the likelihood itself — how sure we are of the number, not how much the world can move.

**Graph.** Propositions + links. A DAG after removing `reflexive` links; reflexive links unroll in time (INV-6). Has exactly one hypothesis and ≥1 terminal (INV-9). Immutable once created; changes are branches.

## The multiverse

**Intervention.** One operation on a graph:
- `do(n, value, at?)` — assert. Cuts the incoming links `n` has **at the moment the edit is applied**; a link inserted later is live. A timed assertion — `do(H, at=Oct 1)` says H holds from the 1st, not that H is sealed for ever. Ancestors unchanged (INV-3). This is what a hypothesis is.
- `observe(n, value)` — learn. Updates ancestors as well as descendants. Distinct verb in the UI.
- `insert(node, links[])` — "…but X happens." Adds a proposition and its links.
- `retune(link, strength)` — the user disagrees with a number.
- `refine(n → children[])` — split a proposition into finer sub-propositions; their combined likelihood must equal the original's (they *marginalize* back to `n`, INV-10). The brainstorm's "search deeper lines".
- `believe(n, belief)` — record the user's own belief on `n`. Lives in the branch so it replays and diffs; never alters `model` or `market` beliefs; not propagated in v1 (D8, INV-11). Propagating a user's world is a stretch (see `probes/`).

**Branch.** A named, ordered list of interventions over a base graph. A branch *is* a patch. Branches compose by concatenation; `apply(g, [])` is `g` (INV-5). Branches may have a parent branch.

**World.** A base graph with a branch applied and beliefs propagated. Replayable from `(base_id, branch, seed)` (INV-5, NFR-2). The base world is the empty branch.

**Diff.** Between two worlds: per proposition, `unchanged` · `shifted` (with before → after) · `added` · `killed`; plus a ranked list of terminal deltas and a one-line natural-language summary. **`killed` means forced false, and nothing else** (decided 2026-09-17) — never "its number got small", and never "no path reaches it from the hypothesis any more", which is a fact about the *path* and is reported by the Inspector's path bar in those words. The ranking is the size of the move times the weakest provenance weight on the **best-backed route** from a differing edit's subject to that ending: over every such route, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest. Two factors; range width and agreement are columns beside it and are never multiplied in.

**Version of the map.** One coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind: every claim's likelihood drawn from its own stated range at once, never every low end together. The engine runs two thousand versions and eight worlds under each. The range on a computed number is the spread across versions; a change is read version by version, never by whether two ranges overlap.

**Agreement.** The share of versions of the map in which a change moved the same way. Computed, never self-reported. A claim counts as `shifted` when it moved by .005 or more **and** agreement is at least 90%; agreement is then shown as its own column beside the change, never multiplied into the ranking. **On screen that column is headed *same direction*** (decided 2026-09-17), and the width column beside it is headed *how firm*; the field names stay `agreement` and `range_width`. Keeping the word *agreement* off this screen leaves it free for stack 04's run-to-run number. Stack 04 may compute a second agreement number — how far several independent generation runs agreed on a claim's likelihood (decision record 0014 defers that question). Same idea, same rule; wherever both could be meant, say which.

**Locality.** An intervention changes only what is still connected to its subject in the graph the edit leaves behind (INV-4). Which claims those are depends on the operation, because the operations leave behind different graphs: `do` cuts the target's incoming arrows, so only the target and its descendants remain connected to it; `observe` cuts nothing, so its ancestors — and what those ancestors cause — are connected too. The per-operation **affected set** table in `multiverse/interventions.md` is the operational form, and the property test computes the set from the shape of the graph. The product's central correctness claim.

## Sensitivity and drill-down

**Sensitivity sweep.** One-at-a-time flip of every proposition; record Δ on each terminal.

**Invalidation.** The proposition whose flip most damages a terminal *and* resolves before it *and* is publicly observable (INV-14). This is the stop-loss. **Take-profit** is the symmetric case. **Unhedgeable**: sensitive but not observable in time; listed, never used as a stop.

**Tail.** A low-probability, high-magnitude proposition. Listed in its own strip with a suggested hedge; never averaged into an expected value.

**Probe** (stretch). A modeling resource attached to one proposition: `monte_carlo` · `bayes_subnet` · `persona_redteam`. Output re-enters the graph as a `simulated` belief with its own rationale.

**Value of information.** How much the trade depends on a proposition × how uncertain it is; ranks where a probe is worth its cost.

## The finale

**Thesis.** The compiled trade: `hypothesis`, `horizon`, `legs[]` (instrument, direction, size, driving proposition, model p, market p, edge), `entry`, `invalidation`, `take_profit`, `distribution` (p10/p50/p90, CVaR₅, max drawdown, P(ruin)), `tails[]`, `caveats` (weakest links, unhedgeable, crowding).

**Strategy export.** A declarative JSON rendering of a thesis with graph references justifying each leg; the shape a downstream trading agent could ingest.

## Surfaces

**Workbench.** The main screen: canvas + world-state strip + Inspector + tail strip + thesis dock.
**Tile.** A proposition's on-canvas card. **Port.** A typed input/output on a tile. **Wire.** A link's on-canvas rendering. **Inspector.** The persistent side panel; never a modal. **Delta rail.** The ranked terminal-delta list beside a diff; its two side columns are headed **how firm** (the width of the new number's range) and **same direction** (the share of versions of the map that moved the same way — the field called `agreement`; on screen the word *agreement* is kept free for stack 04's run-to-run number). **Launchpad.** The empty state with the four seeded examples.

## Interface words

The six operations keep their code names in code, in the wire format and in this document — `do`, `observe`, `insert`, `retune`, `refine`, `believe` — and none of those words appears on screen. These are the words the user reads. Change a button here first, then everywhere else.

| Code name | The button | The badge afterwards | What the interface says it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `do` | **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** | "Take this as given, and do not tell me what caused it" |
| `observe` | **This happened** | **Happened · date** | "This is news — update what came before it too" |
| `insert` | **Add a claim**, hinted as "…but this also happens" | **Added** | A claim and its arrows arrive together |
| `retune` | **Change this push** | **Retuned** | "You moved this arrow from +0.7 to +0.3" |
| `refine` | **Split this claim** | **Split** | The finer claims add back up to the one they replace |
| `believe` | **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge | Your number sits beside the model's and the market's |

One more badge is **derived**: no button produces it. **Retracted · date · by "…"** appears on a claim that was supposed true and has since been pushed back down by a later edit — what was holding this up was removed. It names the edit responsible and the day it landed (UX-14; the mechanism is in `multiverse/interventions.md`).

## Words for a number that is not there

An empty slot never shows a blank, a zero or a placeholder: it shows words and, one hover or one click away, a reason. These are the words; change them here first.

| Where | On the tile | The reason, read in the Inspector and on the chip's hover |
|---|---|---|

| No market price, on an `event` or the `hypothesis` | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim." |
| No market price, on a `not_tradeable` ending | **no market**, with the claim's own stored reason **on the tile** — that reason is a finding, not boilerplate | the same stored reason |
| No number of your own yet | **—** and *add yours* | "You have not given a number for this claim." |
| Nothing has been computed | **no engine yet** | "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet." |

## Words we do not use

61	5. Every number's origin can be named in one click, and no empty slot has been filled in — a number nobody computed is an absence with a reason.

It borrows one thing from mood boards: you can pin, group, and annotate tiles. It borrows nothing from component-library defaults — a template look is a veto condition.

Workbench · Tile · Port · Wire · Inspector · Delta rail · World-state strip · Launchpad · Level of detail.

## Invariants this part owns

| ID | Statement |
|----|-----------|
| INV-8 | Any displayed path shows the multiplied-out likelihood of its steps beside the narrative headline |
| INV-12 | No information is encoded in hue alone: every direction has a glyph, every tail a texture, every provenance a mark — a three-step origin mark at the wire's tail, never the stroke, which says the kind of push and nothing else |

## Chapters

| Chapter | Covers | Written in |
|---------|--------|-----------|
| [`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md) | Tile anatomy, port types, wire encodings, the chip at a wire's midpoint | stack 03b — written, canvas built |
| [`layout-and-zoom.md`](layout-and-zoom.md) | Automatic layered layout, stable incremental re-layout, level of detail by zoom | stack 03b — written, canvas built |
| [`diff-view.md`](diff-view.md) | Ghost overlay of two worlds in a shared layout, the delta rail, A ⇄ A′ toggle | stack 03b — written, canvas built |
| [`inspector.md`](inspector.md) | The persistent side panel: rationale, sources, base rate, three beliefs, "falsified if" | stack 03b — written, canvas built |
| [`color-motion-type.md`](color-motion-type.md) | The color law, the three budgeted animations, typography | stack 03b — written, built bar the number-roll, which has nothing to roll until a number changes |
| [`keyboard-and-access.md`](keyboard-and-access.md) | Keyboard map, outline view for screen readers, reduced motion, contrast | stack 03b — written, canvas built |
| `streaming-growth.md` | How the map draws itself during generation | stack 04 — not written |

**"Built" here means drawn, not fed.** The canvas reads the stored example from `GET /api/fixtures/hormuz`; it does not yet ask the engine's world routes. So every chapter's *drawing* rules are built and tested, and every number a chapter says the engine would compute is on screen as an absence with its reason — "no engine yet". Joining the two is the first job of stack 04, and no component changes when it happens.

## The worked example

Every chapter in this part works its examples on one map: the Strait of Hormuz, served by `GET /api/fixtures/hormuz` and written out, with a reason beside every number, in `backend/src/katalyst/fixtures/hormuz.py`. That file is the source of truth; this table is the cast, so a chapter can say "B" and be understood.

| Letter | Kind | The claim, in the fixture's words |
|---|---|---|
| **H** | hypothesis | The Strait of Hormuz reopens to unrestricted commercial transit. |
| **C** | event | Lloyd's war-risk insurance premium for Gulf transits falls below 0.4%. |
| **B** | event | Brent crude settles below $68 for five sessions. |
| **R** | event | OPEC+ announces output restraint. |
| **M1** | market | A Polymarket contract "Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31" resolves YES. |
| **M2** | market | The energy fund XLE underperforms the S&P 500 fund SPY by more than 3% over 20 trading days. |
| **N1** | not tradeable | Omani-mediated United States-Iran talks resume publicly. |
| **S** | event — added by the branch | A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory. |

**Eight arrows on the base map.** `H → B`, `H → C`, `H → N1`, `C → B`, `B → M1`, `B → M2`, `R → B`, and one that feeds back: `B → R`, a *reflexive* arrow — a market reacting on the world it measures — which always carries a delay. `R → B` is the only one that pushes against its target. `H → N1` is the only one the model merely asserted; the rest are argued.

**One branch,** labelled "Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck" (`br_hormuz_then_strike`), with three edits in order: suppose H is true from Oct 1; add S with three arrows, `S → B`, `S → C` and `S → H`, all pushing against their targets; suppose S is true from Oct 2. Because `S → H` was added *after* H was supposed, it is live — which is what lets the strike retract the strait's opening, and what UX-14's badge exists to say.

## Visual review checklist

Kent vetoes a template-looking interface on sight, so every screenshot is checked for the template first. The chapters cite these lines by number; decision record 0007 promises this list lives here. A "no" on any line sends the work back.

1. Nothing looks like a component library's defaults — no rounded blue button, no drop shadow, no system font stack, no default focus ring.
2. There is no spinner, no pop-up, and no dialog that has to be dismissed.
3. Converted to greyscale, the screenshot still reads: every arrow still says what kind of push it is and where it came from, every direction still reads up or down, every tail still shows as texture (INV-12 — nothing is carried by hue alone).
4. No number shows more than two significant figures, and none is missing its range.
5. Every number's origin can be named in one click, and no empty slot has been filled in — a number nobody computed is an absence with a reason.
6. The map is layered left to right; it is not a hairball of crossings.
7. No text is below 11 pixels, and none is under 4.5 to 1 contrast, in either theme.
8. The tile is 280 pixels wide and on the 8-pixel grid — measured, not eyeballed.
9. Tabbing through the whole screen with the keyboard only, focus is always visible and arrow movement follows the wires.
10. With reduced motion on, the ordering is still there and the tweening is gone.
11. The six buttons and their badges are word for word the Interface words table in [`../vocabulary.md`](../vocabulary.md).
12. A claim that was supposed and then overridden says so on its tile (UX-14).

Decision records behind this part: ADR-0007 (canvas technology), ADR-0014 (what the range under a number means, and how a supposition ends — the words the chips and badges use).

343	   * Not computed here and not carried on the world: it costs a whole extra
344	   * run of the map per arrow, so the engine works one out only when a wire is
345	   * asked about. Until then — and always, in this build, because that route
346	   * does not exist yet — the slot holds its absence and the wire's chip reads
347	   * the push back in words instead. Never a guessed number.
348	   */
349	  readonly conditional: Slot;
350	  /**
351	   * True when this arrow is a market feeding back on the world. A feedback
352	   * arrow is the one arrow allowed to close a loop, and it is set aside when
353	   * the map is sorted into layers — otherwise there would be no left-to-right
354	   * order to sort it into.
355	   */
356	  readonly reflexive: boolean;
357	  /**
358	   * What an edit did to this arrow. Absent when no edit touched it.
359	   *
360	   * - `added` — an **Add a claim** edit brought it.
361	   * - `cut` — a supposition cut it: "take this as given, and do not tell me what
362	   *   caused it". It is still drawn, faint and dashed, because an arrow that
363	   *   simply vanished would be a change nobody could see.
364	   * - `retuned` — a **Change this push** edit moved its number.
365	   */
366	  readonly change?: "added" | "cut" | "retuned";
367	  /**
368	   * True when this arrow is **not** in the world you are looking at. Drawn faint
369	   * in the same place, so that flipping between the two worlds moves nothing.
370	   *
371	   * A ghost arrow is carried by how faint it is and by nothing else. Its stroke
372	   * is fully spent saying what kind of push it is — dot-dash for a spike that
373	   * fades, solid for a switch that holds, doubled when the push only lasts while
374	   * its cause does — and dashing it to say "other world" as well would leave it
375	   * saying neither clearly.
376	   */
377	  readonly ghost?: boolean;
378	}
379	
380	/**
381	 * One world: a map with its numbers as they stand.
382	 *
383	 * "As they stand" is doing real work. In this pull request the numbers are the
384	 * stored example's own, read from the fixture route. When the engine's world
385	 * route lands they will be computed, and the slots that read as absences today
386	 * will fill in. Nothing here has to change for that to happen, because nothing
387	 * false was written.
388	 */
389	export interface WorldView {
390	  /** Which stored example or map this world was built from. */
391	  readonly baseId: string;
392	  /** What the map is called on screen. */
393	  readonly title: string;
394	  /**
395	   * The day the map is set on, as the map itself writes it: `2026-10-01`.
396	   *
397	   * Every resolve-by date on the map is a span from this day, and an edit the
398	   * reader makes takes effect on it, so the map reads the same whenever it is
399	   * opened. The browser's own clock is never consulted: a supposition dated by
400	   * the reader's time zone would make the same map read differently in two
401	   * places.
402	   */
403	  readonly today: string;
404	  /**
405	   * The branch this world has applied, when it has one.
406	   *
407	   * Absent on the base world, which is the empty branch. What the branch panel
408	   * lists, and what every diff state on the claims above was worked out from.
409	   */
410	  readonly branch?: BranchView;
411	  /** The claim the reader started from. */
412	  readonly hypothesisId: string;
413	  /** Every claim on the map. */
414	  readonly claims: readonly ClaimView[];
415	  /** Every arrow on the map. */
416	  readonly links: readonly LinkView[];
417	  /**
418	   * How many versions of the map the engine ran to produce these numbers.
419	   *
420	   * Absent when nothing was computed — which is every world in this build,
421	   * because the engine's route does not exist yet. It is the one thing that
422	   * tells a belief chip whether its range was *computed* across many versions
423	   * of the map or merely *stated* by whoever wrote the number down, and the
424	   * chip says a different sentence for each. Nothing else reads it.
425	   */
426	  readonly versions?: number;
427	
428	  /**
429	   * Where these numbers came from, in one sentence a reader can check.
430	   *
431	   * It is printed under the map. A world whose numbers cannot say where they
432	   * came from is exactly the state this product refuses to show.
433	   */
434	  readonly origin: string;
435	}
436	
437	/** Which world to read: a base map, optionally with a branch applied. */
438	export interface WorldRequest {
439	  /** The stored example or map to read. */
440	  readonly baseId: string;
441	  /** The branch to apply. Left out, this is the base world. */
442	  readonly branchId?: string;
443	}
444	
445	/* ---- Editing the map: branches, and the six operations ------------------- */
446	
447	/**
448	 * One arrow an **Add a claim** edit brings with it.
449	 *
450	 * Only the two ends, because that is all working out what an edit can reach
451	 * needs. When the map itself supplied the arrow — as the stored example's own
452	 * branch does — the whole arrow is on the branch's `links` as well, and that is
453	 * what gets drawn.
454	 */
455	export interface AddedArrow {
456	  /** The arrow's identifier. */
457	  readonly id: string;
458	  /** The claim the arrow starts at. */
459	  readonly source: string;
460	  /** The claim the arrow ends at. */
461	  readonly target: string;
462	}
463	
464	/**
465	 * One edit in a branch.
466	 *
467	 * The six operations keep their code names — `do`, `observe`, `insert`,
468	 * `retune`, `refine`, `believe` — **in code, in the wire format and in the
469	 * spec, and nowhere on screen.** What the reader sees is the button they
470	 * pressed and the badge it earns, both copied word for word from the shared
471	 * vocabulary. `frontend/src/components/BranchPanel.tsx` is the one place those
472	 * words are written.
473	 */
474	export type Edit =
475	  /** Take this as given, and do not tell me what caused it. */
476	  | {
477	      readonly op: "do";
478	      /** The claim being supposed true or false. */
479	      readonly target: string;
480	      /** True to suppose it holds, false to suppose it does not. */
481	      readonly value: boolean;
482	      /** The day the supposition takes effect, as the map writes a day. */
483	      readonly at: string;
484	    }
485	  /** This is news — update what came before it too. */
486	  | {
487	      readonly op: "observe";
488	      readonly target: string;
489	      readonly value: boolean;
490	      readonly at: string;
491	    }
492	  /** A claim and its arrows arrive together. */
493	  | {
494	      readonly op: "insert";
495	      /** The new claim's identifier on the map. */
496	      readonly claimId: string;
497	      /** The new claim in its own words, which is what the badge quotes. */
498	      readonly words: string;
499	      /** The arrows that attach it. */
500	      readonly arrows: readonly AddedArrow[];
501	    }
502	  /** One number on one arrow moves. */
503	  | {
504	      readonly op: "retune";
505	      /** The arrow whose push is being changed. */
506	      readonly link: string;
507	      /** The new push, signed, on the same scale the arrow carries. */
508	      readonly strength: number;
509	      /** What the push was before, so the panel can read the change back. */
510	      readonly wasStrength: number;
511	    }
512	  /** The finer claims add back up to the one they replace. Not built yet. */
513	  | { readonly op: "refine"; readonly target: string }
514	  /** The reader's own likelihood, beside the model's and the market's. */
515	  | { readonly op: "believe"; readonly target: string; readonly belief: Ranged };
516	
517	/** The four hues a branch may take. Never amber: amber means "the money moves down". */
518	export type BranchHue = "violet" | "teal" | "rose" | "slate";
519	
520	/**
521	 * A named, ordered list of edits over a base map. A branch *is* the edits.
522	 *
523	 * It holds no likelihoods and no results. `claims` and `links` are the drawable
524	 * detail for what an **Add a claim** edit brought with it, when the map
525	 * supplied a whole claim rather than only its words — the stored example's own
526	 * branch does; a claim the reader types does not, and is shown in the branch
527	 * panel rather than drawn as a tile.
528	 */
529	export interface BranchView {
530	  /** This branch's identifier. */
531	  readonly id: string;
532	  /** The name the reader reads. */
533	  readonly label: string;
534	  /** Which of the four hues its lane and its name chip take. */
535	  readonly hue: BranchHue;
536	  /** The edits, in the order they were made. Appended to, never rewritten. */
537	  readonly edits: readonly Edit[];
538	  /** Whole claims an edit added, when the map supplied them. */
539	  readonly claims: readonly ClaimView[];
540	  /** Whole arrows an edit added, when the map supplied them. */
541	  readonly links: readonly LinkView[];
542	}
543	
544	/**
545	 * One ending the edit can reach, as the rail beside the map lists it.
546	 *
547	 * Every number on a row is optional, and before the engine every one of them is
548	 * an absence with its reason. The rail ranks nothing and computes nothing.
549	 */
550	export interface DeltaRow {
551	  /** The ending's identifier on the map. */
552	  readonly claimId: string;
553	  /** The ending in its own words. */
554	  readonly label: string;
555	  /** What kind of ending it is, which is what says whether anything trades. */
556	  readonly kind: ClaimKind;
557	  /** How far the number moved, and the day it moved furthest. */
558	  readonly move: Known<{ readonly from: number; readonly to: number; readonly largestOn: string }>;
559	  /** How firm: the width of this world's own range on the claim. */
560	  readonly rangeWidth: Known<number>;
561	  /** Same direction: the share of versions of the map that moved the same way. */
562	  readonly agreement: Known<number>;
563	}
564	
565	/**
566	 * What the panel beside the map is open on, and what the map draws a ring
567	 * around. One name for one thing: the map, the panel and the keyboard all mean
568	 * the same shape by it.
569	 */
570	export type Selection =
571	  | { readonly kind: "claim"; readonly id: string }
572	  | { readonly kind: "wire"; readonly id: string }
573	  | null;
574

6	 * change in `App.tsx`.

9	export { ApiWorldSource } from "./apiSource";

11	export { branchesOf, FixtureWorldSource, monogramFor } from "./fixtureSource";

 *

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * The world source that reads the stored example the server ships with.
3	 *
4	 * Everything the canvas draws in this build comes through here, from
5	 * `GET /api/fixtures/hormuz`. Not one claim, likelihood, arrow or date is typed
6	 * into the browser. If the server's copy of the example changes, the picture
7	 * changes with it and nothing here needs editing.
8	 *
9	 * **What the numbers are, said plainly.** The stored example's likelihoods were
10	 * written by hand, and the file that holds them says so in its own comments:
11	 * they are illustrative, so the machinery has something honest-shaped to run
12	 * on. They are not computed and this half of the product computes nothing. The
13	 * sentence in `origin` below is what the screen prints under the map, so a
14	 * reader never has to take that on trust.
15	 *
16	 * There is no arithmetic in this file. A likelihood is read from the server and
17	 * carried, untouched and at full precision, to the component that prints it.
18	 */
19	
20	import { readExample } from "../api/client";
21	import type { components } from "../api/schema";
22	import type { FixtureBundle, WorldSource } from "./source";
23	import type {
24	  Absence,
25	  AbsenceKind,
26	  BaseRateView,
27	  BranchHue,
28	  BranchView,
29	  ClaimView,
30	  Edit,
31	  EvidenceClipping,
32	  LinkView,
33	  Slot,
34	  SourceView,
35	  WorldRequest,
36	  WorldView,
37	} from "./types";
38	
39	type Proposition = components["schemas"]["Proposition"];
40	type Belief = components["schemas"]["Belief"];
41	type Evidence = components["schemas"]["Evidence"];
42	type Source = components["schemas"]["Source"];
43	type Branch = components["schemas"]["Branch"];
44	type Graph = components["schemas"]["Graph"];
45	
46	/**
47	 * Turn a likelihood from the server into a filled slot, unchanged.
48	 *
49	 * The three numbers are copied across at full precision. Rounding is a display
50	 * decision and is made once, in the chip that prints them.
51	 */
52	function filled(belief: Belief): Slot {
53	  return { reading: { p: belief.p, lo: belief.lo, hi: belief.hi } };
54	}
55	
56	/** Turn "there is no number here" into the words and the reason for them. */
57	function missing(kind: AbsenceKind, words: string, reason: string): Slot {
58	  const absence: Absence = { kind, words, reason };
59	  return { absence };
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * The single letter that stands for a publication, taken from the host name in
64	 * its own web address.
65	 *
66	 * `https://www.bbc.com/news/...` gives `B`. A leading `www.` is dropped first,
67	 * because every publication has one and it would make every monogram a `W`.
68	 *
69	 * A letter rather than the publication's own icon, deliberately: an icon is a
70	 * request to somebody else's server, and this app draws its first frame without
71	 * making one.
72	 */
73	export function monogramFor(url: string): { monogram: string; host: string } {
74	  let host: string;
75	  try {
76	    host = new URL(url).hostname;
77	  } catch {
78	    // An address we cannot read is not a crash. The clipping still has a line
79	    // to show, and the mark beside it says plainly that there is no host name.
80	    return { monogram: "?", host: "an address we could not read" };
81	  }
82	  const withoutWww = host.startsWith("www.") ? host.slice(4) : host;
83	  const first = withoutWww.slice(0, 1).toUpperCase();
84	  return { monogram: first === "" ? "?" : first, host: withoutWww };
85	}
86	
87	/** Turn one published item into the clipping a tile shows. */
88	function clipping(evidence: Evidence): EvidenceClipping {
89	  const { monogram, host } = monogramFor(evidence.url);
90	  return {
91	    line: evidence.claim,
92	    monogram,
93	    host,
94	    direction: evidence.direction,
95	    url: evidence.url,
96	  };
97	}
98	
99	/**
100	 * Turn one item behind an arrow into the source the panel prints.
101	 *
102	 * `retrieved` is the day *our own retrieval step* pulled the page down. It is
103	 * absent whenever a person typed the address in by hand, which is the case for
104	 * every source in the stored example — and the panel says that in words rather
105	 * than printing a day nobody fetched anything on.
106	 */
107	function source(item: Source): SourceView {
108	  const { host } = monogramFor(item.url);
109	  return {
110	    url: item.url,
111	    title: item.title,
112	    host,
113	    retrieved:
114	      item.retrieved === null || item.retrieved === undefined
115	        ? {
116	            absence: {
117	              kind: "not_said",
118	              words: "—",
119	              reason: "nobody fetched this; a person put the address in by hand",
120	            },
121	          }
122	        : { day: item.retrieved },
123	  };
124	}
125	
126	/**
127	 * How often this kind of thing has happened before — or, when the map records
128	 * no such count, the sentence saying so.
129	 *
130	 * The count is printed as `7 of 9` and never as a rate. Dividing one by the
131	 * other would be this half of the product doing arithmetic on the map's
132	 * numbers, and it would also quietly claim that seven-in-nine is the answer,
133	 * which is exactly what a prior is for and exactly what it is not.
134	 */
135	function baseRate(
136	  proposition: Proposition,
137	): { readonly reading: BaseRateView } | { readonly absence: Absence } {
138	  const stored = proposition.base_rate;
139	  if (stored === null || stored === undefined) {
140	    return {
141	      absence: {
142	        kind: "not_said",
143	        words: "—",
144	        reason: "no reference class recorded for this claim",
145	      },
146	    };
147	  }
148	  return {
149	    reading: {
150	      referenceClass: stored.reference_class,
151	      k: stored.k,
152	      n: stored.n,
153	      sources: stored.sources.map((url) => source({ url, title: url, retrieved: null })),
154	    },
155	  };
156	}
157	
158	/**
159	 * Why a claim has no market number, in the words the shared vocabulary settles.
160	 *
161	 * These three sentences are written here and nowhere else, so that the chip,
162	 * the tile and — later — the panel beside the map cannot drift apart about what
163	 * "no market" means. `spec/vocabulary.md` is their source; change it there
164	 * first and then here.
165	 *
166	 * A claim that *ends* the map without an instrument is the exception, and it is
167	 * handled below: that one has a reason of its own, written down when the map
168	 * was made, and it is a finding rather than a fact about our plumbing.
169	 */
170	const NO_MARKET_REASON: Record<"market" | "event" | "hypothesis", string> = {
171	  market: "no venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff",
172	  event: "no venue quotes this claim",
173	  hypothesis: "no venue quotes this claim",
174	};
175	
176	/** Why this claim has no market number. */
177	function marketAbsence(proposition: Proposition): Slot {
178	  if (proposition.kind === "not_tradeable") {
179	    // A dead end says why it is a dead end, in the map's own words. This is the
180	    // one reason a tile prints for itself, because it is an answer rather than
181	    // an apology.
182	    return missing(
183	      "no_market",
184	      "no market",
185	      proposition.not_tradeable_reason ?? NO_MARKET_REASON.event,
186	    );
187	  }
188	  return missing("no_market", "no market", NO_MARKET_REASON[proposition.kind]);
189	}
190	
191	/** Turn one claim from the server into the claim a tile draws. */
192	function toClaim(proposition: Proposition): ClaimView {
193	  const beliefs = proposition.beliefs;
194	  return {
195	    id: proposition.id,
196	    claim: proposition.claim,
197	    kind: proposition.kind,
198	    resolvesBy: proposition.resolution.by,
199	    resolutionSource: proposition.resolution.source,
200	    resolutionCriteria: proposition.resolution.criteria,
201	    prior: { p: proposition.prior.p, lo: proposition.prior.lo, hi: proposition.prior.hi },
202	    baseRate: baseRate(proposition),
203	    beliefs: {
204	      model: filled(beliefs.model),
205	      user: beliefs.user
206	        ? filled(beliefs.user)
207	        : missing("not_said", "—", "You have not put your own number on this claim yet."),
208	      market: beliefs.market ? filled(beliefs.market) : marketAbsence(proposition),
209	    },
210	    // At most two clippings on a tile; every one of them in the panel beside
211	    // the map, where there is room to read them.
212	    evidence: proposition.evidence.slice(0, 2).map(clipping),
213	    evidenceInFull: proposition.evidence.map(clipping),
214	    // The multiplied-out likelihood of a route from the hypothesis to this
215	    // claim. It is computed on the world and this half of the product renders
216	    // it; there is no world yet, so there is no number, and the bar says which
217	    // route it would have been for and that nothing has worked it out.
218	    pathProduct: missing(
219	      "no_engine",
220	      "no engine yet",
221	      "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet. The likelihood of a whole " +
222	        "chain is multiplied out where the map's numbers are computed, and never here.",
223	    ),
224	  };
225	}
226	
227	/** Turn one arrow from the server into the arrow a wire draws. */
228	function toLink(link: components["schemas"]["Link"]): LinkView {
229	  return {
230	    id: link.id,
231	    source: link.source,
232	    target: link.target,
233	    mode: link.mode,
234	    // Carried across at full precision and never touched. The wire compares it
235	    // against four fixed widths and five fixed bands of words; nothing adds it
236	    // to anything.
237	    strength: link.strength,
238	    lag: link.lag,
239	    shape: link.shape,
240	    halfLife: link.half_life ?? null,
241	    rationale: link.rationale,
242	    sources: link.sources.map(source),
243	    provenance: link.provenance,
244	    // The likelihood of this arrow's target with its source supposed true. The
245	    // engine works one out on request, one arrow at a time, and that route does
246	    // not exist yet — so every arrow in this build carries the absence and the
247	    // wire reads its push back in words instead.
248	    conditional: missing(
249	      "no_engine",
250	      "no engine yet",
251	      "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet. The likelihood with this " +
252	        "arrow's cause supposed true costs a whole extra run of the map, so it is " +
253	        "worked out one arrow at a time, and there is nothing to ask yet.",
254	    ),
255	    reflexive: link.reflexive,
256	  };
257	}
258	
259	/**
260	 * The four hues a branch's lane and name chip may take, in the order they are
261	 * handed out. Never amber: amber already means "the money moves down".
262	 */
263	const HUES: readonly BranchHue[] = ["violet", "teal", "rose", "slate"];
264	
265	/**
266	 * Turn one of the map's own branches into the branch the panel lists and the
267	 * diff view folds on.
268	 *
269	 * A branch holds no claims and no numbers of its own — only the edits. What it
270	 * does carry, when an **Add a claim** edit brought a whole claim with it, is
271	 * that claim and its arrows, so the map has something to draw. A claim the
272	 * reader types has only its words, and the branch panel shows it rather than the
273	 * map.
274	 *
275	 * @param branch The branch as the server serves it.
276	 * @param graph The base map, so that a **Change this push** edit can say what
277	 *   the push was before it moved.
278	 * @param hue Which of the four hues this branch takes.
279	 * @param today The day the map is set on, for an edit that names no day of its
280	 *   own.
281	 */
282	function toBranch(branch: Branch, graph: Graph, hue: BranchHue, today: string): BranchView {
283	  const claims: ClaimView[] = [];
284	  const links: LinkView[] = [];
285	  // biome-ignore lint/suspicious/useIterableCallbackReturn: the six operations are the whole of what a branch can hold — the server's own description of itself says so — so every branch of the switch below returns and the type checker proves it. There is no path out of it without a value, and a default case would be a branch no input can reach.
286	  const edits: Edit[] = branch.interventions.map((made): Edit => {
287	    switch (made.kind) {
288	      case "do":
289	        return { op: "do", target: made.target, value: made.value, at: made.at ?? today };
290	      case "observe":
291	        // Observing carries no day of its own: you can only report what has
292	        // already happened, and the map's window starts on its own first day.
293	        return { op: "observe", target: made.target, value: made.value, at: today };
294	      case "insert":
295	        claims.push(toClaim(made.proposition));
296	        links.push(...made.links.map(toLink));
297	        return {
298	          op: "insert",
299	          claimId: made.proposition.id,
300	          words: made.proposition.claim,
301	          arrows: made.links.map((link) => ({

    branch: Branch | None = Field(

    )
    return _answered(compared, request.base_id)


@router.post("/worlds/conditional", responses=REFUSED)
def read_conditional(request: ConditionalRequest) -> Belief:
    """Give the number on one arrow: its target, with its source **supposed** true.

    Supposed, never observed. "How often do these two show up together" is a
    correlation, and an arrow claims a mechanism; the two disagree whenever a
    third thing caused both, and nothing on the wire would tell the reader which
    they were looking at.

    Args:
        request: Which example, which branch, which seed, and which arrow.

    Returns:
        One likelihood with its range, owned by the model.

    Raises:
        HTTPException: With status 404 when nothing is stored under that name, or
            422 when the branch does not fit the map or the arrow is not on it.
    """
    number = engine.conditional(
        request.base_id,
        request.branch,
        request.seed,
        request.link_id,
        versions=request.versions,
        worlds=request.worlds,
    )
    return _answered(number, request.base_id)


def _answered[Answer](outcome: Answer | list[Violation] | None, base_id: str) -> Answer:
    """Hand back the answer, or turn a refusal into the status that says what happened.

    Three outcomes, and each is somebody's fault in a different place. Nothing at
    all means the name does not match any stored example, which is the caller
    asking for something that is not here: 404. A list of violations means the
    branch does not fit the map, which is a branch the user can still repair: 422,
    with every reason at once. Anything else is the answer.

    Args:
        outcome: What the engine gave back.
        base_id: The name that was asked for, for the sentence when it matches
            nothing.

    Returns:
        The answer, when there is one.

    Raises:
        HTTPException: With status 404 or 422, carrying text a person can read.
    """
    if outcome is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=engine.no_such_example(base_id))
    if isinstance(outcome, list):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=[one.model_dump() for one in outcome])
    return outcome

133	    asArrows(links),
134	    branch.edits,
135	  );
136	
137	  const words = new Map(claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, claim.claim]));
138	  for (const edit of branch.edits) {

140	      words.set(edit.claimId, edit.words);
141	    }
142	  }
143	  const badges = badgesByClaim(branch.edits, {
144	    words,
145	    arrows: new Map(

147	        link.id,
148	        { source: link.source, mode: link.mode, strength: link.strength },

150	    ),

163	    branch,

1	# The diff view — two worlds in one picture
2	
3	## Purpose
4	
5	You supposed the strait reopens. Then you added a strike the next day. Two maps now exist, and one
6	question matters: **what did my edit reach, and what did it provably leave alone?**
7	
8	The diff view answers it in one picture. Both maps are laid out **once**, together, then painted
9	twice in the same coordinates — the new world solid, the old world faint behind it. Nothing moves
10	between them, so every difference you see is a real difference and not a re-layout.
11	
12	Before the engine exists that answer is **structural** — *here is what your edit can reach, and here
13	is what it cannot* — and where a number will later sit, this stack draws **an absence with its
14	reason**: never a blank, never a zero, never a stand-in.
15	
16	This chapter owns the ghost overlay, the delta rail, the A ⇄ A′ toggle and the branch panel — and,
17	because every number slot on the world uses them, the `Known<T>` and `Absence` shapes the whole of
18	`spec/workbench/` reads.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Data model
23	
24	### The seam — `WorldSource`
25	
26	The engine (stack 03a) and the canvas (this stack) are built at the same time. One interface keeps
27	them apart, and it is the only place the canvas learns anything:
28	
29	```ts
30	export interface WorldSource {
31	  /** The base map and its branches, as the fixture route already serves them. */
32	  readBundle(id: string): Promise<FixtureBundle>;
33	  /** One world. Its numbers are OPTIONAL — see `Known<T>` below. */
34	  readWorld(request: WorldRequest): Promise<WorldView>;
35	}
36	```
37	
38	Two implementations, and the screen cannot tell which it has. `FixtureWorldSource` reads
39	`GET /api/fixtures/hormuz` and uses the fixture's stored `beliefs.model` for the **base** world —
40	honest, because the fixture says in its own comments that those are illustrative. `ApiWorldSource`
41	calls `POST /api/worlds` and `POST /api/worlds/diff` once they exist.
42	
43	**For the second world, before the engine, there is no second set of numbers at all.** No committed
44	illustrative world, no hand-written likelihoods, no "illustrative numbers" chip. A number nobody
45	computed is exactly the state a reader cannot trace.
46	
47	### `WorldView` — this stack's own view model
48	
49	`WorldView` lives in `frontend/src/world/types.ts` and is **written by hand**, not generated from
50	`frontend/src/api/schema.ts`, which belongs to stack 03a this cycle. Three kinds of absence need
51	three different sentences, so an absence carries both its kind and its sentence:
52

64	}
65

67	    engine and is never produced here. */
